editorial.body: Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon saw the clouds that loomed over his political career all but disappear Friday. An appellate court acquitted the five-term ma...
editorial.pullQuote: An appellate court acquitted the five-term mayor, removing a major obstacle to his political future.

The ruling gives the ruling party a chance to reform and distance itself from political liabilities.

editorial.titleTr: 서울시장 무죄 평결, 국민의힘 쇄신 기회 마련
summaryTr: 서울시장 오세훈이 항소심에서 무죄 판정을 받아 정치 생명의 법적 위협을 벗었다.
이번 판결은 여당에 정치적 부담을 떨쳐내고 개혁할 기회를 안겨줬다.
오세훈의 무죄 판정은 서울 정치판을 재편할 수 있으며 보수진영의 위상을 강화할 가능성이 있다.
editorial.bodyTr: 오세훈 서울시장의 정치 경력 위에 드리워진 먹구름이 금요일 거의 모두 걷혔다. 항소법원이 5선 의원인 그를 뇌물 수수 혐의로 무죄 판결했기 때문이다.

editorial.titleTr: Prosecutors Mass Resign Over President's Coercive Inspection Order
summaryTr: Ministry of Justice decides on verbal warning and no charges for two prosecutors who collectively walked out
Prosecutors file recusal requests and leave courtroom after witness application is rejected
Editorial: Criticism of compromised fairness due to presidential directive for investigation
editorial.bodyTr: The Ministry of Justice has decided to issue a verbal warning and a no-fault ruling to two prosecutors who walked out of court en masse. The prosecutors left the courtroom after filing a challenge to the judges following the bench's rejection of their witness request. An editorial has criticized the president's directive to personally investigate individual cases, arguing that it raises concerns about fairness and wastes administrative resources.

summaryTr: Nuclear Safety Committee Approves Continued Operation of Kori Units 3 and 4

Safety reinforcement and equipment upgrades required before restart
editorials.bodyTr: The Nuclear Safety Commission approved the continued operation of Kori Nuclear Power Plant Units 3 and 4. With this approval, Units 3 and 4 will now operate until 2034 and 2035 respectively, extending beyond their original design lifespan. While this will help meet electricity demand, thorough facility improvements and safety enhancements must be fully implemented before the plants resume operation.

editorials.titleTr: Democratic Party accelerates push to strip chief justice of investigation referral authority
summaryTr: Democratic Party pushes ahead with state audit of Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae
Growing controversy over separation of powers violation and judicial pressure
Legislation to weaken chief justice nomination power also in progress
editorials.bodyTr: The Democratic Party has decided to proceed with a state investigation into Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae and plans to bring it to a plenary session next month on the 5th. The article notes that a state investigation targeting the chief justice could appear as political retaliation that undermines the separation of powers and puts pressure on the judiciary. Some members of the Democratic Party are also pushing for legislative amendments to require the nomination of twice or more the number of Supreme Court justice candidates, which they said would weaken the chief justice's nomination authority.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] President's Defense Adviser's Reckless Remarks on Unilateral War Powers
summaryTr: Presidential defense advisor sparks controversy by advocating for independent wartime operational control without U.S. consultation
Dangerous idea that undermines the foundation of the Korea-U.S. alliance raises questions about U.S. military support missions
Blue House remains silent as public anxiety over national security continues to grow
editorial.bodyTr: Democratic Party lawmaker Kim Byung-joo, the presidential special adviser on defense policy, stirred controversy when he argued during a National Assembly Defense Committee audit two days ago that if the U.S. fails to cooperate and the timing for transferring wartime operational control is not confirmed at the Korea-U.S. Security Consultative Meeting, the government should declare independent exercise of wartime operational control. Until recently, the government and ruling party had pushed for 2030, during President Lee Jae-myung's term, but then shifted to 2028, within the Trump administration's term. Now they are going further, suggesting that if the U.S. does not accept this demand, South Korea should unilaterally declare the transfer of wartime operational control. Given Kim's position as presidential special adviser, his remarks cannot be dismissed as merely a personal opinion. Unilateral declaration of independent wartime operational control is an extremely dangerous idea that shakes not only the basic framework of the wartime operational control transfer initiative pursued since the Roh Moo-hyun administration, but also the very foundation of the Korea-U.S. alliance. The essence of wartime operational control transfer is that during wartime, a future combined military command led by a South Korean four-star general would be supported by the U.S. military. Should South Korea unilaterally declare independent wartime operational control, there is serious doubt whether the U.S. military would faithfully carry out its mission to support South Korean forces as previously agreed. Moreover, questions could naturally arise within the U.S. about extended deterrence and the necessity of maintaining U.S. forces in Korea. The worst-case security scenario in which the Korea-U.S. Mutual Defense Treaty becomes merely nominal cannot be ruled out. Yet presidential foreign policy adviser Song Young-gil has been making comments detached from reality, saying, "Does our recovery of wartime operational control eliminate cooperation with U.S. forces?" The issue of wartime operational control transfer is neither simply a matter of "timing" nor of "autonomy." With North Korea, armed with nuclear weapons and missiles, designating South Korea as its "primary hostile state," and 40 percent of global military forces concentrated around the Korean Peninsula, it is a matter of "deterrence" and "war-fighting capability" that can best strengthen our security. With such grave awareness of the situation, when there are disagreements between allies during consultations, the right approach is to coordinate and persuade to reach a solution. A unilateral declaration of wartime operational control could be perceived as breaking the established framework, and there is a possibility that the situation could develop in directions no one desires. Yet the presidential office has offered not a word in response to this bombshell statement by the presidential adviser. Public security anxieties continue to grow with each passing day.

editorial.title: The repair gap
editorial.body: AI accelerates attacks; weak oversight leaves Korea’s cyber defenses exposed The government can announce a cyber threat in seconds. It may take days to find out whether anyone has fixed it. South Korea’s latest cyber incidents illustrate the gap between detecting a software weakness and confirming that the systems affected have been repaired. On Thursday, the government raised its private-sector cyber alert from “interest” to “caution,” the second-lowest level in its four-tier system, after two serious vulnerabilities were disclosed in PHP, a programming language widely used for websites and online services. The flaws could let remote attackers run code on affected servers. The alert was justified, but it left a more consequential question unanswered: How many operators could install the fixes, and how many authorities could confirm completion? PHP is only part of the picture. Police say an artificial intelligence-assisted hacking operation targeted more than 90 domestic companies and allegedly stole 8.2 million records containing personal information. The PHP vulnerabilities and the alleged intrusion campaign are separate cases, yet both show how automation can turn a software weakness into a large-scale breach. AI helps researchers examine code for defects; attackers can use similar tools to locate vulnerable systems with less technical expertise than such work once required. The interval between disclosure and exploitation is shrinking. Once a flaw becomes public, attackers can study its details and work backward from a patch before every operator has installed it. Large organizations may employ teams capable of auditing systems and applying updates promptly. A small clinic or online shop whose website was built years ago by an outside contractor may have no comparable capacity. An update could disrupt the service on which its business depends. Digital expansion has often outpaced upkeep. Organizations have added online services without maintaining a reliable record of the software they use or assigning clear responsibility for it. Some older versions no longer receive security updates. Outsourcing can blur responsibility further: A hosting provider may maintain the server while the client remains responsible for an outdated application. Government oversight is also incomplete. During a parliamentary audit, the Korea Internet and Security Agency said it could not determine how widely vulnerable PHP versions remained in use at public institutions or whether all fixes had been installed. The agency also cited limits on its authority to inspect systems directly. That leaves officials able to issue instructions without confirming compliance. Because responsibility is split among agencies and sectors, no single body has a complete view of the systems that remain exposed. Policy should make remediation traceable. Authorities need an up-to-date inventory of software running on critical services, alongside clear responsibility for applying and confirming each fix. When an update is unavailable or a system cannot be repaired promptly, operators need alternatives, such as isolating the vulnerable service until it is secured. Public agencies and private security firms need a reliable channel for sharing threat intelligence, with responsibility for acting on it clearly assigned. Smaller businesses need practical assistance to meet these demands. Government support should help pay for security assessments and obsolete-system replacement, including the technical expertise needed to carry out the work. Companies holding large volumes of personal information should face penalties for persistent security neglect. Incentives should reward sustained investment in maintenance and timely updates. AI can improve detection, but it cannot establish who must act or ensure that anyone does. Every alert should identify who is responsible and require independent confirmation that the repair is complete. Korea should judge its cyber defenses by the interval between warning and verified repair. As AI shortens the time needed to find and exploit software flaws, the government’s central task is to ensure that alerts lead to fixes and that the fixes are confirmed. 정부는 사이버 위협을 초 단위로 공표할 수 있다. 영향을 받은 시스템이 실제로 수리되었는지 확인하는 데는 며칠이 걸릴 수 있다. 한국의 최근 사이버 사건들은 소프트웨어 취약점 적발과 피해 시스템 복구 확인 사이의 간극을 드러내고 있다. 목요일 정부는 민간 부문 사이버 경보를 4단계 중 두 번째 수준인 '주의' 단계로 상향했다. 웹사이트와 온라인 서비스에 널리 사용되는 프로그래밍 언어인 PHP에서 두 가지 심각한 취약점이 공개된 후였다. 이 결함들은 원격 공격자들이 영향받은 서버에서 코드를 실행하도록 할 수 있다. 경보는 정당했지만 더욱 중요한 질문은 답이 나오지 않은 채로 남겨졌다. 얼마나 많은 사업자가 수정 사항을 설치할 수 있고, 얼마나 많은 당국이 완료를 확인할 수 있을 것인가?

PHP는 빙산의 일각일 뿐이다. 경찰에 따르면 인공지능 기반 해킹 작전이 국내 90개 이상의 기업을 대상으로 했으며, 개인정보를 담은 82만 개의 기록을 탈취한 혐의가 있다. PHP 취약점과 침해 캠페인은 별개의 사건이지만, 둘 다 자동화가 소프트웨어 취약점을 대규모 침해로 어떻게 변모시킬 수 있는지를 보여준다. AI는 연구원들이 코드의 결함을 찾는 것을 돕는다. 공격자들도 유사한 도구를 사용해 취약한 시스템을 찾을 수 있으며, 과거보다 훨씬 낮은 기술 수준으로도 가능하다. 공개와 악용 사이의 간격이 점점 좁혀지고 있다. 결함이 공개되면 공격자들은 세부 사항을 연구하고, 모든 사업자가 패치를 설치하기 전에 역으로 추적할 수 있다. 규모가 큰 조직들은 시스템을 감사하고 업데이트를 신속하게 적용할 수 있는 팀을 갖추고 있을 수 있다. 몇 년 전 외부 계약자가 만든 웹사이트를 운영하는 소규모 클리닉이나 온라인 가게는 이에 버금가는 역량을 갖추지 못할 수 있다. 업데이트가 자신의 사업이 의존하는 서비스를 중단시킬 수 있기 때문이다. 디지털 확장이 유지보수를 앞질러왔다. 조직들은 사용 중인 소프트웨어의 신뢰할 수 있는 기록을 유지하거나 명확한 책임을 할당하지 않은 채 온라인 서비스를 추가했다. 일부 구형 버전은 더 이상 보안 업데이트를 받지 않는다. 아웃소싱은 책임을 더욱 모호하게 만든다. 호스팅 제공자가 서버를 유지하면서 클라이언트가 오래된 애플리케이션에 대한 책임을 지게 되는 것이다.

정부 감시도 불완전하다. 국정감사에서 한국인터넷진흥원은 공공기관에서 취약한 PHP 버전이 얼마나 널리 사용되고 있는지, 모든 수정 사항이 설치되었는지 판단할 수 없다고 밝혔다. 또한 시스템을 직접 검사할 권한의 한계도 지적했다. 이는 관리들이 준수 여부를 확인하지 않으면서 지시를 내릴 수 있게 한다. 책임이 여러 부처와 부문에 분산되어 있어 노출된 시스템이 어떤 것인지에 대한 완전한 전망을 가진 단일 기관이 없다.

정책은 복구 과정을 추적 가능하게 만들어야 한다. 당국은 중요 서비스에서 실행 중인 소프트웨어의 최신 목록을 필요로 하며, 각 수정 사항의 적용과 확인에 대한 명확한 책임을 함께 해야 한다. 업데이트를 이용할 수 없거나 시스템을 신속하게 수리할 수 없을 때, 사업자들은 취약한 서비스를 보호될 때까지 격리하는 등의 대안이 필요하다. 공공 기관과 민간 보안 회사들은 위협 정보 공유를 위한 신뢰할 수 있는 채널이 필요하며, 이에 대응할 책임이 명확하게 할당되어야 한다. 소규모 기업들은 이러한 요구를 충족하기 위해 실질적인 지원이 필요하다. 정부 지원은 보안 평가와 구식 시스템 교체 비용을 지원해야 하며, 이를 수행하는 데 필요한 기술 전문성도 포함되어야 한다. 대량의 개인정보를 보유하는 회사들은 지속적인 보안 태만에 대해 벌칙을 받아야 한다. 유지보수와 적시 업데이트에 대한 지속적인 투자를 보상하는 인센티브가 제공되어야 한다. AI는 적발 능력을 향상시킬 수 있지만 누가 행동해야 하는지를 정할 수도, 누군가 그렇게 하도록 보장할 수도 없다. 모든 경보는 책임자를 명시해야 하며, 복구가 완료되었는지 독립적으로 확인할 것을 요구해야 한다. 한국은 경고와 입증된 복구 사이의 간격으로 자신의 사이버 방어를 판단해야 한다. AI가 소프트웨어 결함을 찾고 악용하는 데 필요한 시간을 단축시키면서 정부의 중심 과제는 경보가 수정으로 이어지고 그 수정이 확인되도록 보장하는 것이다.

editorials.title: The repair gap
editorials.body: AI accelerates attacks; weak oversight leaves Korea’s cyber defenses exposed The government can announce a cyber threat in seconds. It may take days to find out whether anyone has fixed it. South Korea’s latest cyber incidents illustrate the gap between detecting a software weakness and confirming that the systems affected have been repaired. On Thursday, the government raised its private-sector cyber alert from “interest” to “caution,” the second-lowest level in its four-tier system, after two serious vulnerabilities were disclosed in PHP, a programming language widely used for websites and online services. The flaws could let remote attackers run code on affected servers. The alert was justified, but it left a more consequential question unanswered: How many operators could install the fixes, and how many authorities could confirm completion? PHP is only part of the picture. Police say an artificial intelligence-assisted hacking operation targeted more than 90 domestic companies and allegedly stole 8.2 million records containing personal information. The PHP vulnerabilities and the alleged intrusion campaign are separate cases, yet both show how automation can turn a software weakness into a large-scale breach. AI helps researchers examine code for defects; attackers can use similar tools to locate vulnerable systems with less technical expertise than such work once required. The interval between disclosure and exploitation is shrinking. Once a flaw becomes public, attackers can study its details and work backward from a patch before every operator has installed it. Large organizations may employ teams capable of auditing systems and applying updates promptly. A small clinic or online shop whose website was built years ago by an outside contractor may have no comparable capacity. An update could disrupt the service on which its business depends. Digital expansion has often outpaced upkeep. Organizations have added online services without maintaining a reliable record of the software they use or assigning clear responsibility for it. Some older versions no longer receive security updates. Outsourcing can blur responsibility further: A hosting provider may maintain the server while the client remains responsible for an outdated application. Government oversight is also incomplete. During a parliamentary audit, the Korea Internet and Security Agency said it could not determine how widely vulnerable PHP versions remained in use at public institutions or whether all fixes had been installed. The agency also cited limits on its authority to inspect systems directly. That leaves officials able to issue instructions without confirming compliance. Because responsibility is split among agencies and sectors, no single body has a complete view of the systems that remain exposed. Policy should make remediation traceable. Authorities need an up-to-date inventory of software running on critical services, alongside clear responsibility for applying and confirming each fix. When an update is unavailable or a system cannot be repaired promptly, operators need alternatives, such as isolating the vulnerable service until it is secured. Public agencies and private security firms need a reliable channel for sharing threat intelligence, with responsibility for acting on it clearly assigned. Smaller businesses need practical assistance to meet these demands. Government support should help pay for security assessments and obsolete-system replacement, including the technical expertise needed to carry out the work. Companies holding large volumes of personal information should face penalties for persistent security neglect. Incentives should reward sustained investment in maintenance and timely updates. AI can improve detection, but it cannot establish who must act or ensure that anyone does. Every alert should identify who is responsible and require independent confirmation that the repair is complete. Korea should judge its cyber defenses by the interval between warning and verified repair. As AI shortens the time needed to find and exploit software flaws, the government’s central task is to ensure that alerts lead to fixes and that the fixes are confirmed. 노동시장 구조 변화로 청년 실업 문제가 심화되는 추세다.
고용 정책 개선이 시급한 상황으로 평가된다.
editorial.stance: 청년 고용난 해소를 위한 구체적 정책 마련이 필요하다
editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Bank of Korea Warns Youth Face Steeper Barriers to Permanent Employment
summaryTr: The Bank of Korea diagnosed that young people are finding it increasingly difficult to enter regular employment.
Youth unemployment problems are intensifying due to structural changes in the labor market.
Improving employment policies is assessed as an urgent priority.
